questions.subdomain: 6.3 Evaluate the compliance of AWS resources
questions.question: A central cloud team must roll out an identical set of AWS Config rules and remediation actions to every member account in the organization. Member account administrators must not be able to change or remove what is rolled out. The rollout must be run from one place for all accounts rather than account by account. Which approach meets these needs?
options: Deploy an organization conformance pack from the management account, so member accounts cannot edit its rules or remediations.
Ask each member account administrator to create the rules from a shared template and keep them current in their own account.
Have each member account deploy the conformance pack itself, and add an SCP that denies changes to the Config rules.
Use service-managed StackSets from the management account to create the rules as ordinary AWS Config rules in each member account.
questions.correct_rationale: An organization conformance pack is deployed centrally and its rules and remediations cannot be modified by member accounts.
distractor_rationales: Member-managed rules are neither central nor protected from change.
Per-account deployment fails the single-rollout requirement even if an SCP protects the result.
Ordinary rules created by StackSets remain editable by member account administrators.
questions.distractor_summary: WA leaves rules editable; WB is per account; X does both.

docLinks.title: Managing Conformance Packs for AWS Config Across all Accounts in Your Organization

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: A company receives files from partners in an S3 bucket. Downstream applications read new objects from that bucket. Each newly uploaded object must be scanned for malware without the company running its own scanning servers. Downstream applications must be unable to read an object until its scan has marked it clean. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Run an open source antivirus engine on an EC2 Auto Scaling group that S3 event notifications trigger, and have it copy clean objects to a second bucket.
Enable GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 on the bucket without tagging, and have the downstream applications poll GuardDuty findings before they read each new object.
Enable GuardDuty S3 Protection on the account, which reviews CloudTrail data events for the bucket and raises findings for suspicious access to new objects.
Enable GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 on the bucket with tagging, and add a bucket policy that denies reads unless the scan-result tag shows the object is clean.
questions.correct_rationale: Malware Protection for S3 scans new uploads with no servers to run, and its scan-result tag lets a bucket policy block reads until an object is clean.
distractor_rationales: This can work, but the company would run and patch its own scanning servers, which it wants to avoid.
Scanning happens, but nothing blocks reads; the applications would have to enforce the result themselves from findings.
S3 Protection analyzes access activity in CloudTrail events; it does not scan object contents for malware.
questions.distractor_summary: WA scans but never blocks reads; WB means running servers; X watches access, not file contents.

docLinks.title: GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: A security operations team watches CloudWatch metrics, log groups, and alarms across a dozen workload accounts in an organization. Analysts must search logs and build dashboards across all the workload accounts while signed in to one central account. The team does not want to copy log data into the central account or switch roles into each workload account. What should the team configure?
options: A CloudWatch dashboard in each workload account that is shared publicly, with the analysts bookmarking every dashboard URL in a browser.
A cross-account IAM role in every workload account that analysts switch into from the central account to open that account's console.
A CloudWatch Logs subscription filter in every workload account that streams each log group into a destination in the central account.
CloudWatch cross-account observability, with the central account set as a monitoring account and each workload account linked as a source account.
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-account observability lets the monitoring account search and chart source account data in place, with no copies and no role switching.
distractor_rationales: Public dashboards expose security data and do not provide cross-account log search from a central account.
Role switching gives access, but the analysts would switch into each account instead of working from one place.
Subscription filters copy log data into the central account, which the team explicitly does not want.
questions.distractor_summary: WA copies data; WB needs role switching; X exposes dashboards publicly and gives no search.

docLinks.title: CloudWatch cross-account observability

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design and implement monitoring and alerting solutions for an AWS account or organization
questions.question: A company uses Security Hub CSPM across an organization with a delegated administrator account and several linked Regions. The security team must decide from one place which standards and controls are enabled in each organizational unit. The settings must apply in the home Region and every linked Region without being configured Region by Region. Which approach meets these requirements?
options: Have each account owner enable the chosen standards and controls through a runbook that the security team publishes for every Region in use.
Turn on central configuration in the delegated administrator account and associate configuration policies with each organizational unit.
Use local configuration in the delegated administrator account and enable the chosen standards in the home Region for each new member.
Create an SCP that denies the Security Hub CSPM disable APIs so that member accounts keep whatever standards they enabled themselves.
questions.correct_rationale: Central configuration lets the delegated administrator set standards and controls per OU with policies that apply in the home and linked Regions.
distractor_rationales: A runbook leaves the work to each owner in each Region, which is the opposite of deciding from one place.
Local configuration does not apply the settings across linked Regions and existing accounts the way policies do.
An SCP can stop changes, but it does not choose or enable the standards and controls for each OU.
questions.distractor_summary: WA pushes work to owners; WB does not span linked Regions; X blocks changes but sets nothing.

docLinks.title: Understanding central configuration in Security Hub CSPM

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: A company sends AWS WAF web ACL logs to a central log store that many analysts can read. Requests carry an authorization header that must not appear in the stored log records. To control storage cost, the company wants to keep log records for blocked requests and drop the rest. How should the security engineer configure logging?
options: Redact the authorization header in the web ACL logging configuration, and keep every record so that analysts can compare blocked and allowed traffic.
Turn off logging on the web ACL and use the sampled requests view in the console to review blocked requests when an analyst needs them.
Redact the authorization header in the web ACL logging configuration and add a log filter that keeps records whose action is block.
Add a log filter that keeps records whose action is block, and have the analysts ignore the authorization header in the records they read.
questions.correct_rationale: Field redaction keeps the header out of the records, and log filtering on the rule action keeps blocked requests and drops the rest.
distractor_rationales: Redaction protects the header, but keeping every record does not meet the cost goal.
Sampled requests are a small sample, not a log of every blocked request.
Filtering cuts volume, but the header would still be written to the shared log store.
questions.distractor_summary: WA leaves the header in logs; WB keeps every record; X stops logging.

docLinks.title: Finding your protection pack (web ACL) records

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design and implement logging solutions
questions.question: A central logging account owns an S3 bucket that receives CloudTrail log files from an organization trail. The bucket policy must allow the CloudTrail service principal to write log files to the bucket. An auditor requires that CloudTrail can write to the bucket on behalf of the organization trail and no other trail. Which bucket policy change meets these requirements?
options: Allow the PutObject action for the CloudTrail service principal, with an aws:SourceArn condition that matches the ARN of the organization trail.
Allow the PutObject action for the CloudTrail service principal on the log prefix, with no condition on which trail is making the write request.
Allow the PutObject action for the management account root principal, with an aws:SourceArn condition that matches the ARN of the organization trail.
Allow the PutObject action for any principal in the organization with aws:PrincipalOrgID, and require SSE-KMS on every object that is written.
questions.correct_rationale: CloudTrail writes as its service principal, and aws:SourceArn on the trail ARN limits those writes to that trail.
distractor_rationales: This lets CloudTrail write, but any trail in any account could use the grant.
CloudTrail delivers as its service principal, so a grant to the root principal does not authorize the deliveries.
This trusts every principal in the organization rather than the one trail, and encryption does not limit the writer.
questions.distractor_summary: WA lets any trail write; WB grants the wrong principal; X trusts the whole organization.

docLinks.title: Amazon S3 bucket policy for CloudTrail

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: An engineer enables access logging on an Application Load Balancer and points it at an existing S3 bucket in the same account. The bucket policy grants Elastic Load Balancing permission to write, yet no log files arrive in the bucket. The bucket's encryption setting is SSE-KMS with a customer managed key, and the company requires nothing more than encryption at rest for the logs. What should the engineer do to start receiving the logs?
options: Change the bucket's encryption setting to SSE-S3, which ALB access logs support, and keep the existing bucket policy grant.
Add a statement to the customer managed key policy that lets the Elastic Load Balancing principal call kms:GenerateDataKey.
Add a bucket policy statement that denies the PutObject action unless the request uses SSE-KMS with the customer managed key.
Turn on S3 Object Lock in governance mode on the bucket, and then disable and re-enable access logging on the load balancer.
questions.correct_rationale: ALB access logs support SSE-S3 for the destination bucket, which still meets the encryption-at-rest requirement.
distractor_rationales: Key policy changes do not help because ALB access logs do not support SSE-KMS buckets.
Requiring SSE-KMS would keep rejecting the log deliveries rather than fix them.
Object Lock controls deletion; it does not address the unsupported encryption setting.
questions.distractor_summary: WA edits a key that ALB logs cannot use; WB enforces the unsupported mode; X is unrelated.

docLinks.title: Enable access logs for your Application Load Balancer - Elastic Load Balancing

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: A security team configures GuardDuty in one Region to export findings to an S3 bucket in a log archive account. The bucket policy allows GuardDuty to write, but saving the export configuration fails with a KMS error. The bucket is in the detector's Region, and the export uses a customer managed KMS key that the team created in a second Region. What should the team do to fix the export?
options: Remove the KMS key from the export settings so that GuardDuty writes findings with no key, and keep the export as it is.
Use a customer managed key in the detector's Region for the export and add a key policy statement that allows GuardDuty to use that key.
Move the export bucket to the second Region, and keep that key without adding any statement for GuardDuty to its key policy.
Add a key policy statement to the second-Region key that allows GuardDuty to use it, and keep exporting to the same bucket.
questions.correct_rationale: The bucket and key must share a Region, and GuardDuty needs key policy permission to use the key.
distractor_rationales: GuardDuty findings export requires a KMS key; removing the key from the settings does not remove that need.
The Regions would then match, but GuardDuty still has no permission to use the key.
Granting GuardDuty access helps, but a key in another Region than the bucket still fails.
questions.distractor_summary: WA keeps the Region mismatch; WB keeps the missing key grant; X drops a required key.

docLinks.title: Exporting generated GuardDuty findings to Amazon S3 buckets

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Troubleshoot security monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
questions.question: An EventBridge rule sends GuardDuty findings to an SQS queue that a remediation worker reads. The rule matches findings, but no messages reach the queue and the rule shows failed invocations. The queue uses SSE-KMS with the AWS managed key for SQS, and security policy requires the queue to stay encrypted with KMS. What should the security engineer do?
options: Encrypt the queue with a customer managed key and allow the EventBridge service principal to use that key in its own key policy.
Change the queue to SSE-SQS with SQS-owned encryption keys, and keep the queue policy that already allows EventBridge to send.
Add a queue policy statement that allows the EventBridge service principal to call sqs:SendMessage, and keep the AWS managed key.
Edit the AWS managed key for SQS so that its key policy allows the EventBridge service principal to call kms:GenerateDataKey.
questions.correct_rationale: A customer managed key lets the key policy grant EventBridge access, which an AWS managed key's policy cannot be edited to do.
distractor_rationales: SSE-SQS would deliver, but it does not keep the queue encrypted with KMS as the policy requires.
Send permission alone does not help while EventBridge cannot use the queue's KMS key.
AWS managed key policies cannot be edited, so this grant is not possible.
questions.distractor_summary: WA edits a key that cannot be edited; WB leaves KMS; X fixes the queue policy, not the key.

docLinks.title: Troubleshooting Amazon EventBridge

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: An incident response team has changed the EventBridge rules that start its containment automation. It wants to resend last week's real security events to the same event bus to confirm the new rules react correctly. Which feature supports this?
options: An EventBridge archive on the event bus, followed by a replay of the archived events from last week to that same bus.
CloudTrail Event history filtered to last week, with each event downloaded and reviewed by hand against the new rules.
EventBridge Pipes that read the security events from a queue and pass each one through an enrichment step to the rules.
An EventBridge Scheduler schedule that sends one sample security event to the event bus every few minutes for a week.
questions.correct_rationale: An archive keeps the received events, and a replay resends them to the original event bus to exercise the rules.
distractor_rationales: Event history shows API events for review; it does not resend events to the bus.
Pipes connect a source to a target; they do not resend past events that the bus already received.
A schedule sends synthetic events, not last week's real events.
questions.distractor_summary: Pipes move new events; Scheduler sends synthetic ones; Event history is for reading.

docLinks.title: Archiving and replaying events in Amazon EventBridge

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: A company signs in to its AWS accounts through IAM Identity Center with a third-party IdP. Responders must keep access to a few critical accounts if IAM Identity Center becomes unavailable during an incident. The company does not want long-term IAM user credentials stored for responders, and the plan must work when it is needed. What should the security team prepare?
options: Add a second permission set in IAM Identity Center with administrator access, and assign it to each responder in every account.
Configure SAML 2.0 federation from the IdP directly to the critical accounts with emergency roles, and test it before any disruption.
Create IAM users with console passwords in each critical account, and store their credentials in a sealed envelope for the responders.
Plan to configure SAML 2.0 federation from the IdP to the critical accounts after IAM Identity Center becomes unavailable.
questions.correct_rationale: Direct SAML federation to the critical accounts avoids long-term credentials, and preparing it in advance means it works during the outage.
distractor_rationales: Another permission set still depends on IAM Identity Center, which is the service that is down.
This works during an outage, but it relies on long-term IAM user credentials that the company rejects.
Setting up federation during the outage is too late; the configuration must exist before the disruption.
questions.distractor_summary: WA stores long-term credentials; WB is set up too late; X depends on the failed service.

docLinks.title: Set up emergency access to the AWS Management Console

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design and test an incident response plan
questions.question: Analysts triage findings in Security Hub CSPM. A Lambda function can isolate an EC2 instance named in a finding. The function must run for a finding when an analyst decides it should, from the Security Hub CSPM console. The function must not run for findings that analysts have not chosen, even when those findings are critical. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Create a Security Hub CSPM insight that groups critical findings by instance, and have analysts copy each instance ID into the function.
Create an automation rule in Security Hub CSPM that sets the workflow status to notified for each critical finding as it arrives.
Create a Security Hub CSPM custom action and an EventBridge rule that matches its custom action ID and targets the Lambda function.
Create an EventBridge rule that matches every imported finding with a severity label of critical and targets the Lambda function.
questions.correct_rationale: Analysts send a chosen finding to the custom action, and the rule on that action ID runs the function for that finding alone.
distractor_rationales: An insight groups findings, but copying IDs by hand is not a console-triggered response.
Automation rules update finding fields; they do not run the isolation function from an analyst's choice.
This runs for every critical finding, including ones analysts never chose.
questions.distractor_summary: WA fires on all critical findings; WB only updates fields; X needs manual copying.

docLinks.title: Security Hub CSPM event types in EventBridge

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: GuardDuty reports that a Lambda function is sending data to a known malicious domain after a dependency was compromised. Responders must stop all new invocations of the function at once while they investigate. The function code, configuration, and versions must be kept unchanged as evidence for the investigation. What should the responders do first?
options: Delete the function and its versions so that no invocation can run, and redeploy it from the source repository later.
Set the function's reserved concurrency to one so that invocations run one at a time and responders can watch each one as it runs.
Set the function's reserved concurrency to zero so that every new invocation is throttled while the function stays in place.
Upload a new deployment package that returns at once, so that every new invocation runs the harmless replacement code.
questions.correct_rationale: Zero reserved concurrency throttles all invocations without altering the code, configuration, or versions.
distractor_rationales: Deletion stops invocations but destroys the evidence the responders must keep.
Concurrency of one still lets the compromised code run.
Replacing the package changes the function's code, which must stay unchanged.
questions.distractor_summary: WA destroys evidence; WB changes the code; X still runs the code.

docLinks.title: Configuring reserved concurrency for an Event Function

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: A database password stored in Secrets Manager was committed to a public code repository an hour ago. The secret already has a rotation function and a schedule that rotates it every thirty days, and applications fetch the secret at run time. The leaked password must stop working as soon as possible without an outage for the applications. What should the security engineer do?
options: Delete the secret with a recovery window, and create a new secret with a new password for the applications to fetch.
Start an immediate rotation of the secret in Secrets Manager, which changes the password in the database and in the secret.
Change the password directly in the database, and update the secret value later during the next application release window.
Shorten the rotation schedule to every day so that the next scheduled rotation replaces the leaked password in the database.
questions.correct_rationale: An immediate rotation replaces the password at once in both places, and applications pick up the new value at run time.
distractor_rationales: Deleting the secret breaks the applications that fetch it by name, and the old password still works in the database.
The applications would fetch the stale secret and fail until the secret is updated.
A shorter schedule still waits for the next rotation, so the leaked password keeps working for a while.
questions.distractor_summary: WA waits for the schedule; WB breaks fetches; X breaks apps and leaves the password valid.

docLinks.title: Set up automatic rotation for non-database AWS Secrets Manager secrets

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: During an investigation, responders find that a security group on a production instance was opened to the internet at some point last week. They need to see each configuration state the security group passed through over the week. They also need to see which API calls, and by which principals, changed the group, from the same view. Which view should the responders use?
options: The VPC Flow Logs for the instance's network interface, queried for accepted inbound traffic from internet addresses.
The AWS Config compliance timeline for a rule that checks for unrestricted inbound access on security groups in the account.
The CloudTrail Event history for the account, filtered by the security group ID, which lists the API calls made against it.
The AWS Config resource timeline for the security group, filtered to show both configuration events and CloudTrail events.
questions.correct_rationale: The resource timeline shows each recorded configuration of the group and can show the CloudTrail events that changed it in one view.
distractor_rationales: Flow logs show traffic, not the configuration changes or who made them.
A rule's compliance timeline shows pass or fail changes, not the full configurations and the callers.
Event history shows the API calls, but not each resulting configuration state of the group.
questions.distractor_summary: WA lacks configuration states; WB shows traffic; X shows compliance only.

docLinks.title: Viewing Compliance History for your AWS Resources with AWS Config

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Respond to security events
questions.question: An application behind CloudFront is protected by an AWS WAF web ACL. Responders see credential stuffing from a changing group of addresses. Responders must block the addresses they identify during the incident across several web ACLs that protect related sites. Adding a newly found address must not require editing the rules in every web ACL each time. Which approach meets these requirements?
options: Add a rate-based rule to each web ACL, and lower its threshold each time responders find more of the addresses.
Add a new blocking rule with an IP match statement to every web ACL each time responders identify another address.
Add the addresses to the network ACLs of the origin subnets, and update each network ACL as responders find more.
Create one IP set, reference it from a blocking IP set rule in each web ACL, and add new addresses to that IP set.
questions.correct_rationale: One shared IP set referenced by a block rule in each web ACL means only the set changes when a new address appears.
distractor_rationales: A rate-based rule acts on request rates, not on a list of identified addresses.
This blocks the addresses, but it edits rules in every web ACL each time, which must be avoided.
Traffic reaches the origin from CloudFront, so origin network ACLs do not see the attacker addresses.
questions.distractor_summary: WA edits every web ACL; WB sees CloudFront addresses; X limits rates, not addresses.

docLinks.title: Creating and managing an IP set in AWS WAF

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: A retailer uses AWS WAF on its storefront. The common level of the Bot Control rule group is already in place. Scrapers now rotate addresses and send browser-like user agents, so they do not identify themselves as bots. The retailer wants AWS WAF to detect these bots with browser interrogation and behavior signals without writing its own detection. What should the security engineer do?
options: Keep the common protection level of the Bot Control rule group, and add a rule that blocks requests with browser user agents.
Add a rate-based rule that blocks any single address that sends more than a set number of requests in a short period.
Change the Bot Control rule group to the targeted protection level, which adds detection for bots that do not self identify.
Add the Amazon IP reputation list managed rule group, which blocks addresses that are known sources of bot traffic.
questions.correct_rationale: The targeted level uses browser interrogation, fingerprinting, and behavior heuristics to catch bots that do not self identify.
distractor_rationales: The common level labels self-identifying bots, and blocking browser user agents would also block real shoppers.
Rotating addresses defeat a per-address rate limit.
Reputation lists catch known bad addresses, not rotating scrapers with browser-like behavior.
questions.distractor_summary: WA blocks real users; WB is beaten by rotation; X lists known addresses only.

docLinks.title: AWS WAF Bot Control

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: A company runs an internal web application on EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application has no login code. Employees must authenticate with the corporate identity provider, which is OIDC compliant, before any request reaches the instances. The development team will not add authentication code or an agent to the application. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Put an AWS WAF web ACL on the load balancer with a rule that blocks requests that lack a corporate session cookie.
Restrict the load balancer security group to the corporate office address ranges and leave the listener rule unchanged.
Add an OIDC client library to the application on each instance so that it redirects unauthenticated users to the corporate provider.
Add an authenticate-oidc action to the HTTPS listener rule before the forward action, using the corporate identity provider.
questions.correct_rationale: The listener authenticates users with the OIDC provider before forwarding, so requests reach the instances already authenticated.
distractor_rationales: Checking for a cookie does not authenticate the user with the identity provider.
Network restrictions limit where requests come from, not who the user is.
This authenticates users, but it adds code to the application, which the team will not do.
questions.distractor_summary: WA adds code; WB checks a cookie, not a user; X limits networks, not identities.

docLinks.title: Authenticate users using an Application Load Balancer - Elastic Load Balancing

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for network edge services
questions.question: A company exposes a REST API through API Gateway. Partner servers call it from fixed public address ranges. Internal services call the same API from a VPC through an interface VPC endpoint for API Gateway. All other callers must be denied before any authorizer or backend runs, and no proxy may be added in front of the API. What should the security engineer configure?
options: A security group on the VPC endpoint that allows the partner address ranges, along with the internal services in the VPC.
A Lambda authorizer that checks the caller's source address against the partner ranges and returns a deny for other addresses.
An API Gateway resource policy that allows the partner address ranges and the VPC endpoint and denies requests from any other source.
An AWS WAF web ACL that allows the partner address ranges, attached to an Application Load Balancer placed in front of the API.
questions.correct_rationale: A resource policy can allow source address ranges and specific VPC endpoints and deny every other caller at the API.
distractor_rationales: The endpoint security group controls VPC traffic; partner calls over the internet never pass through it.
An authorizer runs as part of the request, so other callers would reach it rather than being denied first.
This adds a proxy in front of the API, which is not allowed.
questions.distractor_summary: WA lets callers reach the authorizer; WB never sees partner calls; X adds a proxy.

docLinks.title: Control access to a REST API with API Gateway resource policies

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: A team runs many Lambda functions and wants Amazon Inspector findings on them. Findings must cover vulnerable packages in the function dependencies and code flaws such as injection and hardcoded secrets in the custom code. The team wants Amazon Inspector to provide both, with no scanning tools added to the build pipeline. What should the team activate?
options: Lambda standard scanning and then Lambda code scanning in Amazon Inspector for the account.
Amazon ECR enhanced scanning on the repository that stores the function packages for the team.
Lambda code scanning in Amazon Inspector for the account, with Lambda standard scanning left deactivated.
Lambda standard scanning in Amazon Inspector, with a static code analysis tool added to the build pipeline.
questions.correct_rationale: Standard scanning covers dependency vulnerabilities, and code scanning, which needs standard scanning first, covers custom code flaws.
distractor_rationales: ECR scanning covers container images, not zip-packaged function code.
Code scanning cannot be activated without standard scanning.
This covers the code, but it adds a tool to the pipeline, which the team does not want.
questions.distractor_summary: WA skips a prerequisite; WB adds a pipeline tool; X scans images, not functions.

docLinks.title: Scanning AWS Lambda functions with Amazon Inspector

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot security controls for compute workloads
questions.question: An ECS cluster runs tasks on EC2 container instances in awsvpc network mode. Each task has its own task IAM role. A review found that a task could reach the instance metadata service and obtain the container instance role credentials. Tasks must keep using their task role credentials while being blocked from the instance metadata service. What should the security engineer do?

Set the ECS_AWSVPC_BLOCK_IMDS agent configuration variable to true on the container instances in the ECS cluster.
Remove the task IAM roles from the task definitions so that the tasks have no credentials that could be reused.
Require IMDSv2 on the container instances so that every task must request a session token before reading metadata.

Removing task roles breaks the tasks' own access, which must continue.

Nitro Enclaves attestation, which lets the enclave prove its identity and code so that KMS key policy conditions can rely on it.
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, which records every shell session that administrators open on the instance.
EC2 instance profiles, which give the instance a role whose KMS permissions any process on the instance can use at once.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Design and troubleshoot network security controls

A stateful domain list rule group that denies the cloud storage domain names in outbound HTTPS requests from the VPC.
A TLS inspection configuration on the firewall so that outbound HTTPS is decrypted, inspected by stateful rules, and re-encrypted.
VPC Flow Logs with all fields for the firewall subnets, analyzed in Athena for unusually large outbound HTTPS transfers.

distractor_rationales: This inspects content, but it adds proxy instances, which is not allowed.

Flow logs record connection metadata, not decrypted content.

VPC Reachability Analyzer, with a path from the application server's network interface to the database's network interface.
VPC Flow Logs on both network interfaces, reviewed for rejected records after the engineer sends test connections.

distractor_rationales: Network Access Analyzer checks access against a scope, here internet paths, not this one server-to-database path.
Traceroute sends test traffic and does not name the misconfigured component.
Flow logs need test traffic and time to collect, which the engineer wants to avoid.

Associate every VPC with one route table and propagate every VPC to it, then rely on security groups to stop workload traffic between the attached VPCs.
Associate workload VPCs with an isolated route table that receives shared services routes, and propagate workload VPCs to a shared route table.
Associate workload VPCs with an isolated route table that receives every workload VPC route, and propagate shared services to it.

distractor_rationales: Peering works but abandons the transit gateway design rather than configuring it.
One flat route table lets every workload VPC route to every other.
Propagating workload routes into the table the workloads use lets them reach each other.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: A customer-facing web application uses an Amazon Cognito user pool for sign-in. Create an IAM SAML identity provider in the AWS account, and have the application call AWS STS to assume a role for each employee.
Create a Cognito identity pool for the employees, and have the application use the identity pool credentials in place of user pool tokens.
Create user pool accounts for the employees with temporary passwords, and email each employee a sign-in link for the application.

Identity pool credentials replace the user pool tokens that the application must keep using.
Temporary passwords create separate user pool passwords, which must be avoided.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: A company uses IAM Identity Center with its built-in identity store. MFA is set to context-aware, so users on remembered devices are not prompted. Auditors now require every user to complete MFA at every sign-in, including from devices that were used before. Users who have not registered an MFA device must be blocked from signing in until they register one. Which settings meet these requirements?
options: Set MFA prompting to every time users sign in, and set the action for users without a registered device to block their sign-in.
Set MFA prompting to every time users sign in, and let users without a registered device register a device when they next sign in.
Keep context-aware MFA prompting, and set the action for users without a registered MFA device to block their sign-in.
Keep context-aware MFA prompting, and attach an IAM policy that denies actions when aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent is false.

distractor_rationales: This prompts every time, but it lets users without a device sign in to register rather than blocking them.
Context-aware prompting still skips MFA on trusted devices, even with the block setting enabled.
Context-aware prompting still skips the MFA step at sign-in for trusted devices.
questions.distractor_summary: WA keeps the trusted-device gap; WB lets deviceless users in; X keeps the gap at sign-in.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: Administrators need SSH access to Linux instances in private subnets of a VPC. The security team is removing the bastion hosts from the public subnets. The instances must stay without public IP addresses, and the VPC must not gain an internet gateway path to them. Access must be controlled with IAM permissions, and the administrators must not have to run or patch any bastion instance. Which solution meets these requirements?

Create an EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint in the VPC, allow SSH from it in the instance security groups, and grant IAM access to use it.
Create a site-to-site VPN to the office, share one SSH key pair with the administrators, and allow SSH from the office range.
Assign Elastic IP addresses to the instances, restrict SSH in their security groups to the office range, and use IAM to manage the keys.
questions.correct_rationale: The endpoint gives private SSH reach to instances with no public address, with IAM controlling its use and no bastion to manage.
distractor_rationales: This keeps a bastion instance that the team would still have to run and patch.
A VPN with a shared key pair does not use IAM permissions to control access.
Elastic IP addresses give the instances public addresses, which the first requirement rules out.
questions.distractor_summary: WA adds public IPs; WB keeps a bastion; X uses shared keys, not IAM.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: A batch service calls an internal API that is protected by a JWT authorizer, which trusts tokens issued by an Amazon Cognito user pool. The batch service runs with no human user, so it must obtain tokens without any user signing in. The API must be able to restrict the batch service to read operations through scopes carried in its tokens. Which approach meets these requirements?
options: Define a resource server with custom read scopes, and give the batch service an app client with a secret that uses the client credentials grant.
Create a Cognito identity pool for the batch service, and have it get temporary AWS credentials and signs each API call with them.
Give the batch service an app client with a secret that uses the client credentials grant, and check its client ID in the API code.
Create a Cognito user for the batch service, and have it sign in with a stored password to get tokens that carry read scopes.
questions.correct_rationale: Client credentials with a secret need no user sign-in, and resource server scopes let the authorizer limit the service to reads.
distractor_rationales: An identity pool gives AWS credentials, not user pool tokens with scopes for the JWT authorizer.
This gets tokens without a user, but there are no custom scopes for the API to restrict on.
A stored user password means a user signs in, which the first requirement rules out.
questions.distractor_summary: WA needs a user; WB lacks scopes; X yields IAM credentials, not JWTs.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authentication strategies
questions.question: A platform team runs the same payments application in several Amazon EKS clusters. Pods use the node instance role today to call AWS services. Each application's pods must receive their own IAM role, rather than every pod on a node sharing the node role. Adding the application to a new cluster must not require editing the trust policy of its IAM role each time. Which approach meets these requirements?
options: Use IAM roles for service accounts, and add each new cluster's OIDC provider to the trust policy of the application role.
Use EKS Pod Identity, creating an association between the application role and its service account in each cluster that runs it.
Attach the payments permissions to the node instance role in each cluster, and use taints so payments pods run on their own nodes.
Store access keys for an IAM user in a Kubernetes secret in each cluster, and mount the secret into the payments pods.
questions.correct_rationale: Pod Identity gives pods a role through their service account, and identical associations work in new clusters without trust edits.
distractor_rationales: This gives per-application roles, but each new cluster needs a trust policy edit for its OIDC provider.
The pods still use the node role, so permissions are tied to nodes rather than to the application.
Long-lived access keys in secrets are not a role for the pods and are not a sound credential practice.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A shared data lake bucket is used by many analytics teams. The bucket policy has grown long and every team change needs a review of the whole policy. Each team must get its own entry point to the bucket, with permissions it can change without editing the bucket policy. The central team must keep control at the bucket level so that access is granted through those entry points and not directly. Which approach meets these requirements?
options: Create an access point for each team with its own policy, and keep adding each team's permissions to the bucket policy as well.
Create an access point for each team with its own policy, and set the bucket policy to delegate access control to the bucket's access points.
Split the bucket policy into one statement block per team, and let each team edit its own statement block in the bucket policy.
Create a separate IAM role for each team with S3 permissions, and grant the roles access to the bucket in the bucket policy.
questions.correct_rationale: Delegation lets each access point policy govern its team, while the bucket policy keeps access flowing through access points.
distractor_rationales: Access points help, but adding each team's permissions to the bucket policy keeps the long shared policy.
Teams would still be editing the bucket policy, which the first requirement rules out.
Roles named in the bucket policy still grow that policy and give direct access, not access through entry points.
questions.distractor_summary: WA keeps bucket policy growth; WB edits bucket policy; X grants direct access.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A sales table in the AWS Glue Data Catalog is queried through Amazon Athena. Regional analysts share one table that has a customer email column. Each regional group of analysts must see rows for its own region and no rows from other regions. Analysts must not see the email column, and the table must not be copied into separate per-region tables. Which approach meets these requirements?
options: Grant each group Lake Formation SELECT on the table with the email column excluded, and ask analysts to filter by region in queries.
Create Athena views per region that drop the email column, and grant each group IAM access to its view in the workgroup.
Create Lake Formation data filters per region with a row filter expression that excludes the email column, and grant each group its filter.
Run a nightly job that writes each region's rows without the email column to its own table, and grant each group its own table.
questions.correct_rationale: A data filter combines a row filter with column exclusion on the same table, so each group sees its region without the email column.
distractor_rationales: Column exclusion hides email, but nothing stops analysts reading other regions' rows.
Views in Athena do not stop direct reads of the underlying table through IAM, so rows and email stay reachable.
Per-region copies hide the rows and column, but the table must not be copied.
questions.distractor_summary: WA lacks row limits; WB copies data; X does not secure the base table.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A company uses IAM Identity Center with its corporate directory. Twenty project teams need access to their own resources in shared accounts. The company wants a single permission set for all project engineers, rather than one permission set per team. Each engineer must reach the resources tagged with their own team's project and no other team's resources. Which approach meets these requirements?
options: Create one IAM user per engineer in each shared account, and attach a policy that lists the resources for that engineer's team.
Create one permission set per team with a policy that names that team's resource ARNs, and assign each team its own permission set.
Create one permission set that grants access to all project resources, and rely on the teams to use their own resources.
Enable attributes for access control with the directory's team attribute, and write the permission set policy to match it to resource tags.
questions.correct_rationale: ABAC matches a user's team attribute to resource tags, so one permission set gives each engineer only their team's resources.
distractor_rationales: IAM users per account bypass Identity Center and multiply the policies to manage.
Per-team permission sets restrict access, but the company wants one permission set.
One permission set is used, but nothing stops engineers reaching other teams' resources.
questions.distractor_summary: WA uses many permission sets; WB over-grants; X bypasses Identity Center.

questions.question: A mobile app stores each user's records in a DynamoDB table whose partition key is the user ID from Amazon Cognito. Users get credentials through an identity pool. Each user must be able to read and write the items whose partition key is their own Cognito identity, and no other user's items. The control must be enforced by the IAM policy on the role, not by checks in the app code. Which policy element meets these requirements?
options: A condition with StringEquals on dynamodb:Attributes set to the Cognito identity ID variable of the caller for every request.
A condition with ForAllValues:StringEquals on dynamodb:LeadingKeys set to a fixed value that the app passes for each user.
A Resource element that names the table ARN, with the app code adding a filter on the user ID to each query it sends.
A condition with ForAllValues:StringEquals on dynamodb:LeadingKeys set to the Cognito identity ID variable of the caller.
questions.correct_rationale: LeadingKeys with ForAllValues compares the partition key to the caller's identity variable, so each user reaches their own items.
distractor_rationales: dynamodb:Attributes limits which attributes are returned, not which partition keys a user can reach.
A fixed value does not tie the key to each caller's own identity.
A filter in app code is not enforced by IAM, which the second requirement demands.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Design, implement, and troubleshoot authorization strategies
questions.question: A Lambda function processes object-created notifications from one S3 bucket in the same account. A review flags the function policy. The S3 service principal must be allowed to invoke the function for notifications from that specific bucket. Notifications from any other bucket, including buckets in other accounts with the same name pattern, must not be able to invoke it. Which change to the function's resource-based policy meets these requirements?
options: Grant lambda:InvokeFunction to the S3 service principal with a condition on aws:SourceArn for a wildcard matching the bucket name pattern.
Grant lambda:InvokeFunction to the S3 service principal with no conditions, and rely on the bucket's notification setup to limit callers.
Grant lambda:InvokeFunction to the account root principal, and add a condition on aws:PrincipalOrgID for the company's organization.
Grant lambda:InvokeFunction to the S3 service principal with conditions on aws:SourceArn for the bucket ARN and aws:SourceAccount for the account.
questions.correct_rationale: SourceArn pins the bucket and SourceAccount pins the owning account, so the S3 principal can invoke for that bucket and no other.
distractor_rationales: A wildcard on the name pattern lets other matching buckets, including ones elsewhere, invoke the function.
With no conditions, any bucket's notifications could invoke the function through the S3 principal.
Naming the account root does not grant the S3 service principal the invoke permission it needs.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 Design and implement controls for data in transit
questions.question: A company needs private TLS certificates for internal services and wants a root CA with subordinate CAs, without running its own CA servers. Which service supports this?

AWS Key Management Service asymmetric keys, used by each service to sign its own certificate for internal use.
AWS Private CA, used to set up a private root CA and subordinate CAs that issue the internal certificates.
AWS Secrets Manager secrets that hold self-signed certificates created by each team for its internal service.
questions.correct_rationale: Private CA builds private root and subordinate CA hierarchies as a managed service, with no CA servers to run.
distractor_rationales: Public certificates need publicly resolvable domain validation and do not form a private CA hierarchy.

Self-signed certificates in secrets do not create a root and subordinate hierarchy.

Enable mutual TLS on a custom domain name with the CA bundle as the trust store, and keep the execute-api endpoint for partner testing.
Disable the execute-api endpoint, and require an API key in a usage plan that each partner sends with every request to the API.
Require a Lambda authorizer that reads a certificate header sent by the partner, and keep the execute-api endpoint for partner testing.

API keys identify callers but do not verify X.509 client certificates against the CA.

At-rest encryption protects stored data, not traffic on the network.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design and implement controls for data at rest
questions.question: A company must encrypt DynamoDB tables at rest with a key it creates and controls, including its key policy and rotation. Which encryption option meets this?

An AWS managed key for DynamoDB, which is stored in the account but whose key policy AWS sets and manages.
A customer managed KMS key that the company creates in its account and selects for the table's encryption at rest.
An AWS owned key, which DynamoDB uses to encrypt the table without any key appearing in the company's own account.

Create a blue/green deployment whose green environment is encrypted with the customer managed key, then switch over to it.

A dump and load reaches encryption, but rebuilding the data needs the long outage the requirements rule out.

questions.question: A team finds that a shared Amazon EFS file system used by build servers was created unencrypted. Other teams in the account also create file systems. The data on the unencrypted file system must move to storage that is encrypted at rest. From now on, principals in the account must not be able to create unencrypted EFS file systems. questions.subdomain: 5.3 Design and implement controls to protect confidential data, credentials, secrets, and cryptographic key materials
questions.question: A team turns on automatic rotation for a customer managed KMS key that encrypts years of archived data. What happens to data encrypted before the rotation?

It must be re-encrypted under the new key material before rotation completes, or the archived data cannot be decrypted.
It stays readable for a grace period after rotation, after which the old key material is deleted by KMS.

KMS keeps prior key material, so old ciphertext needs no re-encryption.

questions.subdomain: 5.3 Design and implement controls to protect confidential data, credentials, secrets, and cryptographic key materials
questions.question: An application runs in two Regions for disaster recovery. Its database credentials are a secret in Secrets Manager in the primary Region. The application in the second Region must read the same credentials from a secret in its own Region, kept in step with rotation in the primary. If the primary Region is lost for a long time, the team must be able to manage the secret in the second Region on its own. Which approach meets these requirements?

Store a copy of the credentials in an encrypted Parameter Store parameter in the second Region, and read it there.

distractor_rationales: Reading the primary Region's secret fails when that Region is lost and is not a local read.
A hand-updated copy is not kept in step with rotation.
A parameter copy is not updated by rotation and is a separate store to manage.
questions.distractor_summary: WA is not local; WB drifts on rotation; X is unsynchronised.

Remove the delegated administrator, then ask each member account owner to activate Inspector again and associate their account with the new administrator.
Export all Inspector findings to an S3 bucket in the new account and recreate the organization so that the new account becomes the management account.

questions.question: A company uses Amazon Macie to find sensitive data in S3 and wants new findings sent to its ticketing system through an HTTPS endpoint. Create an EventBridge rule that matches Macie finding events and targets the endpoint, and add a second rule that also forwards the archived suppressed findings.

Turn on the audit log type for control plane logging on the production cluster and leave the API server, scheduler, and other log types off.

lessons.title: Turning on detection once for the whole organization
body: Detection questions in a multi-account setting usually ask how to cover every account, including accounts created next month. Look for the delegated administrator pattern: a security tooling account administers GuardDuty for the organization, and auto-enable set to cover all member accounts brings in new and existing accounts without per-account work. An organization trail created from the management account does the same for CloudTrail, logging events for the management account and all member accounts.

The second axis is where findings and logs end up. Security Hub CSPM cross-Region aggregation replicates findings from linked Regions to one home Region, so analysts work from one view. Amazon Security Lake ingests security logs and converts them to Apache Parquet in the OCSF schema, which suits teams that want a normalized data lake rather than a findings console. Macie automated sensitive data discovery evaluates the bucket inventory and samples representative objects, which keeps cost down compared with scanning everything.

When logging is configured but nothing arrives, check the role chain before the feature. VPC flow logs publishing to CloudWatch Logs need a role whose trust policy lets the flow logs service assume it. API Gateway execution logging needs the cloudWatchRoleArn account setting in each Region where logging is turned on, so a second Region fails silently until it is set there too.

lessons.title: Containing first, then finding the root cause
body: Incident response questions reward the action that actually stops the activity now. A security group change does not immediately interrupt connections it is already tracking, so containing an instance under active attack can need a network ACL deny on the subnet, which is stateless. For a role whose temporary credentials leaked, the revoke active sessions feature attaches an inline policy that denies all actions for credentials issued before the chosen time, which cuts off the stolen sessions without deleting the role.

Investigation questions separate tools that record from tools that analyze. Athena can query CloudTrail log files in place by pointing a table LOCATION at the log prefix in S3, which answers who did what with SQL. Amazon Detective helps analyze and investigate findings and identify the root cause of suspicious activity, which suits a question about relationships between entities over time rather than one API call.

Preparation questions test automation and rehearsal. Systems Manager Automation runbooks can call custom Python or PowerShell through the aws:executeScript action, and Security Hub CSPM automation rules update findings that match criteria, such as lowering severity for a sandbox account. AWS FIS runs controlled fault experiments with stop conditions tied to alarms, so a team can rehearse a response safely against a real workload.

lessons.title: Placing the control at the right layer
body: Infrastructure questions usually name a layer without saying so. Request floods from individual clients point to an AWS WAF rate-based rule, which counts requests and rate limits sources that send too fast. Keeping users from bypassing CloudFront to reach an S3 origin points to origin access control with a bucket policy that allows that distribution. For a load balancer origin, CloudFront can add a secret custom header and the listener forwards only requests that carry it.

Compute questions focus on removing standing access paths. Session Manager opens shell sessions with no inbound ports, bastion hosts, or SSH keys. Requiring IMDSv2 on an instance makes IMDSv1 calls fail, which closes a common credential theft route. Amazon Inspector set as the scanning service for a private ECR registry checks pushed container images for software vulnerabilities.

Network questions split blocking from discovering. A custom network ACL on a subnet can explicitly deny an address range, which security groups cannot do because they support allow rules alone. AWS Network Firewall with a stateful domain list controls outbound traffic by name. Network Access Analyzer finds unintended paths, such as from the internet to a database, from a scope you define, which answers a review question rather than a blocking one.

lessons.title: Removing long-term credentials and scaling permissions
body: Many identity questions are really asking how to stop using long-term access keys. A CI system with an OIDC token can assume a role through an IAM OIDC identity provider. Servers in a data center that hold certificates from a private authority can get role credentials through IAM Roles Anywhere with that authority as a trust anchor. A workforce in an external identity provider signs in to many accounts through IAM Identity Center, with SAML for sign in and SCIM for provisioning users and groups.

Session details matter. A presigned S3 URL signed with temporary credentials expires when those credentials expire, whatever expiry was requested, which explains links that fail early from a Lambda role. Requiring MFA for an API action uses the aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition on the allowing statement. Cognito adaptive authentication asks for an additional factor when the risk level rises, rather than on every sign in.

Authorization questions test which tool limits what. A permissions boundary sets the maximum permissions an identity policy can grant, which lets developers create roles without escalating. Attribute-based access control lets one policy scale by matching principal tags to resource tags. A third party assuming a role should pass a unique external ID in the trust policy condition. IAM Access Analyzer identifies resources shared with an external entity.

lessons.title: Matching the protection to the threat model
body: Data in transit questions often hide the leg of the connection. An Application Load Balancer security policy is the negotiation configuration between clients and the load balancer, so tightening client protocol versions happens on the listener, not on the targets. Private connectivity to Amazon S3 splits by where the client sits. A gateway endpoint is a route table target for traffic from inside the VPC, while an interface endpoint has private addresses that on-premises clients can reach over Direct Connect or Site-to-Site VPN.

Data at rest questions turn on who must be unable to delete or read. S3 Object Lock in compliance mode stops any user, including the root user, from overwriting or deleting a protected version, while governance mode can be bypassed with special permissions. AWS Backup vault lock offers the same two modes for recovery points. A KMS key in a CloudHSM key store keeps non-extractable key material in a cluster the customer owns and manages, while services keep calling KMS.

Key material and secrets questions ask where material comes from and who rotates it. Importing key material into a KMS key created without material lets a company use keys generated outside AWS. Managed rotation for Aurora master credentials updates the secret and the database with no Lambda function. A CloudWatch Logs data protection policy can be set for all log groups in an account so sensitive values are masked, including in new groups.

lessons.title: Governing many accounts from the center
body: Organization policy questions test which principals a policy reaches. SCPs restrict principals in member accounts but do not affect users or roles in the management account, which is why workloads should not run there. Resource control policies restrict principals external to the organization from accessing resources in member accounts, which builds a central data perimeter that does not depend on each team editing resource policies. Centralized root access lets the security team delete root user credentials from member accounts while keeping privileged tasks available.

Deployment at scale questions ask what happens when accounts and resources change. A service-managed StackSet with automatic deployment adds stacks to accounts that join a target OU and removes them from accounts that leave. Firewall Manager sets protections once and applies them across accounts and resources, including new accounts and load balancers, which a shared web ACL or a one-time StackSet cannot do.

Compliance questions separate detection, remediation, and audit evidence. AWS Config remediation runs Systems Manager Automation documents, so a noncompliant resource can be fixed automatically without custom code. AWS Audit Manager automates evidence collection to assess whether controls operate effectively, while AWS Artifact provides AWS compliance reports about AWS itself.
